key_insight: ERCPMP-Gx introduces a much-needed endoscopic image and video dataset focused on colorectal polyposis, linking visual findings with histopathology and genomic information. This enables AI systems to move beyond single-polyp detection toward syndrome-level characterization and more clinically useful classification.
problem_solved: Most public endoscopic datasets are organized around isolated sporadic polyps and do not connect the polyposis phenotype to pathology or genomic context. This paper addresses the gap by supporting early identification and more accurate classification of hereditary polyposis syndromes, which are important precursors to colorectal cancer.
method: Curates an endoscopic image and video dataset centered on colorectal polyposis cases rather than individual sporadic lesions.
Pairs visual data with histopathological and genomic characterization to create richer multimodal labels.
Targets downstream AI use cases such as syndrome classification, phenotype analysis, and risk-aware clinical decision support.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset enables multimodal learning that is more aligned with real clinical questions than standard polyp detection benchmarks. It can support better generalization, richer supervision, and development of models for hereditary disease characterization and surveillance planning.

paper_title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
paper_authors: Zahra Ghaffari, Massih Bahar, Mojgan Forootan, Ali Darvishi, Hamidreza Bolhasani
